reviews.review: I keep trying to give this game a chance but it keeps letting me down ^^; crashes constantly on my computer, is visually unimpressive for the most part, and the story really is not gripping me. might be worth it for someone but not me :(

ive been playing for about 30 minutes so here goes.

the first mission is like a mashup of 'arriving on halo' and 'two betrayals' from 'halo ce' and 'requiem' from halo 4.
its like  'arriving on halo' because you land on an alien planet and explore the wild, although not nearly as open.
its like 'two betrayals' because you go to multiple alien structures from one side of the map to the other, although not nearly as open.
its like 'requiem' because when you go outside the crash zone you see a giant forerunner tower.

the colonists are awakened for their exo planet then remnant vessel or derelict ship crashes into some crystals that are in orbit around the exo planet the tempest sustains some damage from it then you and some other drop ships get sent to the exo planet. when you get there you and the other drop ships crash which causes a ton of casualties. when you wake up you see a giant alien tower then head into the wilds to find survivors of the crash.
the visuals for this game are amazing. seeing the colonists sci fi cryostasis room then the exo planet then the alien architecture then the wildlands of the exo planet is so cool.

This is my favorite Mass Effect game. It has improved almost all aspects from the original trilogy, and is probably the most immersive space game I have played.

Some things that I like:

[list]
    [*] Beautifully designed interior environments
    [*] Large and beautiful outdoor worlds
    [*] Fun vehicle exploration, finally with a vehicle that is fun to drive
    [*] Punchy combat, with noticeably different weapons and powers
    [*] Much better menus and UI that does not get in the way
    [*] Much nicer and smoother navigation between planets
    [*] More fluent and natural conversations - less chit chat than the originals
    [*] More natural and humoristic side conversations between NPCs
    [*] More realistic outposts, that feel lived in and functional
    [*] More natural side mission design - there is no feel of "fetch quests" and side missions integrate nicely with the main story
    [*] Clear and appealing exploration-oriented story-line
    [*] Generous amount of content - many hours of game play without the feel of it being dragged out
[/list]
